subject: Order form redlines: IP, feedback license, and runtime usage controls
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@lumenai.com>, Procurement <procure@lumenai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Order form redlines: IP, feedback license, and runtime usage controls

Hi Emily / Lumen procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Attached is our redlined Order Form (OrderForm_LumenAI_v3_redlines.pdf) and a short summary of the key open items so legal/procurement can triage quickly. TL;DR: we can accept many of the commercial terms but need to land concrete language on three IP/usage points before we can sign:

1) Output ownership: Lumen is asking for assignment of output title for generated content. We are not comfortable with a broad assignment that would prevent Redwood from using aggregated outputs to maintain safety/quality. Proposed: customer ownership of their outputs for their productization, plus a narrow feedback license for Redwood limited to safety, debugging, and model quality improvement (no retraining on identifiable customer content without explicit consent).

2) Training/data use: Lumen currently requests a catch-all training license. We propose to carve this out entirely and provide a process for opt-in training where Lumen can allow aggregated/anonymized telemetry to be used after a review and additional commercial terms.

3) Runtime usage & hosted vs. private: need explicit runtime usage controls (who can run which models where) and telemetry/retention limits for logs and prompts. Our suggested retention default is 30 days for debug logs, with options for extended retention via enterprise settings.

Attachments: order form redline, and a short redline_summary_table.csv that maps asks -> proposed language.

Next steps: can you confirm whether Lumen can accept (A) feedback license limited to improving Redwood services (non-exclusive, non-sublicensable), and (B) an opt-in training path rather than a default training license? If you prefer, we can have Laura (legal) propose concrete wording.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: OrderForm_LumenAI_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf), redline_summary_table.csv (csv)

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@lumenai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@lumenai.com>, Legal Team <legal@lumenai.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines: IP, feedback license, and runtime usage controls

Hi Karthik —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline. Legal and procurement are already looking. A couple quick reactions from the business side so we can keep momentum:

- We understand Redwood's need for a safety/quality feedback loop, but Lumen’s product team needs stronger rights to use outputs for internal product improvement (not necessarily a transfer of title).
- We cannot accept a complete ban on training; at minimum we need a permissive, controlled right to derive model improvements from aggregated customer outputs and telemetry. We are open to guardrails (aggregation, de-identification, contractual auditability).
- On runtime: we need to be explicit that we can run inference in our VPC for latency-sensitive product features (we expect that to be in the Dedicated or Private deployment section of the Order Form).

I’ve attached a short counter (LumenAI_proposed_counter.docx) that shows the customer's preferred language and a small table with required internal approvals. Legal will send a formal note but wanted to surface these product constraints early.

Thanks —
Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Product, LumenAI
emily.chen@lumenai.com

Attachments: LumenAI_proposed_counter.docx (docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@lumenai.com>, Procurement <procure@lumenai.com>, Legal Team <legal@lumenai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Order form redlines: IP, feedback license, and runtime usage controls

Laura / Markus —

Looping you in for legal/ops position. Emily's note makes it clear Lumen needs some ongoing ability to use outputs and telemetry for product improvement; they want that to be a default, not opt-in. Two asks for legal to prepare guidance on:

1) Output ownership vs. feedback license: we should propose narrow language that preserves customer productization rights while allowing Redwood to (a) store and process outputs for debugging, (b) use aggregated and de-identified signals to improve models, and (c) not use identifiable customer content for model retraining without explicit opt-in and separate commercial terms. Please draft a clause we can send directly to Lumen.

2) Runtime usage and deployment permissions: define what running in a customer VPC means operationally (no custody of models, limited telemetry access, SLA differences). Also confirm what telemetry/retention defaults we can offer without escalating to Sales leadership.

I attached redline_summary_table.csv with itemized asks. Would appreciate suggested clause language and risk posture (accept / counter / escalate).

If legal wants to propose a middle-ground, maybe offer: 
- Feedback license: non-exclusive, limited to improving Redwood services, restricted to aggregated/de-identified data;
- Telemetry retention: default 30 days (extendable to 90 with enterprise add-on);
- Training: opt-in only, commercial uplift applies.

Happy to jump on a quick call with Laura/Markus and Lumen legal if you think that helps.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachments: redline_summary_table.csv (csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@lumenai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redlines: IP, feedback license, and runtime usage controls

Emily / Karthik —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the redlines and Lumen’s counter. Below is a pragmatic legal stance and proposed compromise language you can share with Lumen legal. We think this will protect Redwood's operational needs while addressing Lumen's product concerns.

Proposed negotiating posture:
- Aim to agree a non-exclusive "Feedback License" rather than assignment of output title. This satisfies Lumen's need to use outputs while preserving Redwood's ability to operate and improve its services.
- Make training on identifiable customer content opt-in only, with explicit consent and a separate SOW/pricing schedule.
- Offer clarified runtime definitions for Dedicated/Private deployments in the Order Form; include a short operational appendix that explains telemetry access, model custody, and SLA differences.

Suggested language (short form):
"Feedback License: Customer hereby grants Redwood a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to use Customer-provided prompts, outputs, and telemetry solely to (i) diagnose and remediate service incidents, (ii) evaluate and improve the safety and quality of Redwood services, and (iii) develop aggregated or de-identified models and metrics. Redwood will not use Customer-identifiable content to train models for commercial release without Customer's prior written consent and separate commercial terms."

"Training; Opt-in: Customer may, at its sole election and subject to a separate written agreement, permit Redwood to use aggregated and de-identified Customer data for model training. Any such training will be documented in an addendum and include additional compensation and data handling commitments."

Telemetry & Retention:
- Default retention for debug logs and call transcripts: 30 days.
- Enterprise retention up to 90 days available with an additional fee or as set in the Dedicated/Private deployment schedule.

If Lumen insists on assignment of output title as a mandatory term, escalate to Sales leadership for an exec approval conversation (this is a potential deal-killer without commercial uplift).

Next steps I recommend: share the language above with Lumen legal and propose a 30-minute call next week to resolve the telemetry/retention numbers and confirm the opt-in training flow. If they accept the Feedback License + opt-in training model, we can finalize the Order Form with the runtime appendix and move to signature.

Happy to edit wording further based on Lumen legal's reply.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
